parsed.notes: Reviewed all 5 assertion rows. Lens A refutes only quote-fidelity defects; treatment was recorded but not substantively attacked.

reasons: The lake identity record is United States v. Jones, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2012-01-23, docket 10-1259.
The official citation in the lake record is 565 U.S. 400, with parallel citations 132 S. Ct. 945 and 181 L. Ed. 2d 911, matching the content-page citation data.

defect.evidence_quote: the Katz reasonable-expeetation-of-­privacy test has been added to, not substituted for, the common-law trespassory test.
defect.problem: The quoted pin-409 text is not character-faithful to the disclosed cached opinion text, and the lake record itself marks this pinpoint quote_fidelity as mismatch.
defect.proposed_fix: Refresh or replace the quote with text that is faithful to the disclosed opinion source, or paraphrase the Katz/trespass-test point instead of presenting it as verbatim.

reasons: The content/lake quote uses cleaned Markdown text: "the *Katz* reasonable-expectation-of-privacy test...".
The disclosed text contains different characters and markup, including "reasonable-expeetation-of-­privacy" and commas inside the emphasized phrases.
residual_risks: The legal proposition is supported, but the direct quote should not be treated as character-faithful on this record.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use a paraphrase for the Katz point unless a clean, verified source text is loaded.

defect.evidence_quote: We have no doubt that such a physical intrusion would have been considered a <page-number citation-index="1" label="405">*405</page-number>“search” within the meaning of the Fourth Amendment when it was adopted.
defect.problem: The pin-404a quote is substantively supported but not character-faithful: the page/lake quote uses straight single quotes around 'search' while the opinion text uses curly double quotation marks and crosses the 404-405 page break.
defect.proposed_fix: Change the direct quote to match the disclosed text's quotation marks, or paraphrase the sentence instead of presenting it as verbatim.

reasons: The cited passage exists and supports the trespass-search proposition.
The verbatim quote is not character-faithful because the quoted word is rendered as 'search' in the content/lake quote but as “search” in the disclosed opinion text.
residual_risks: Only quote fidelity is refuted; support and pincite appear otherwise sound.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Retain the 404-05 pincite but normalize the quote to the disclosed text.

defect.evidence_quote: We hold that the Government’s installation of a GPS device on a target’s vehicle,<footnotemark>2</footnotemark> and its use of that device to monitor the vehicle’s movements, constitutes a “search.”
defect.problem: The pin-404 payload quote is not an opinion quote; it splices page content/heading text and does not match the actual 565 U.S. at 404 holding sentence.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace pin-404 with the actual holding sentence from the opinion, preserving the footnote marker or avoiding a direct quote across it.

reasons: The lake pin-404 quote is "within the meaning of the Fourth Amendment. ## Rule Yes — under a trespass-based theory of the Fourth Amendment.", which is not the opinion's holding sentence.
The disclosed text at page 404 contains the correct holding sentence beginning "We hold that...".
residual_risks: The page's legal rule is supported, but the pin record is corrupted and should not be used as a verbatim quote source.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Regenerate pin-404 from the opinion text rather than from surrounding content-page Markdown.

reasons: The treatment payload matches the lake treatment fields: field_i_validity good_law, as_of_content 2012-01-23, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, varies_by_point false, and the same scope note.
Treatment/currency is outside Lens A, so no treatment finding is raised.
residual_risks: Treatment currency not assessed under this lens.
